subject: middle children
one_liner: Buy a place at Sunday lunch. Being noticed is a separate upgrade.
brand_voice_notes: Write as a ticket retailer calmly selling adult middle children a place in their own family. Start with wanting to be included, then show what happens to the purchased entitlement. Use ordinary family situations and plain functional labels. Treat birth-order habits as the fictional customers' behavior, without presenting them as psychological facts. Apply the frozen anti-ai-slop skill throughout: no em dashes, corporate enthusiasm, throat-clearing or explanatory endings.
demo_screen_concept: A ticket-booking screen for Sunday Lunch with Mum & Dad, Sunday at 1 pm, at the family home. The event header sits above a selectable dining-table seating map, ticket categories and an order summary. Choose the reserved chair beside Mum and confirm the booking. A family update announces that Ben is bringing the baby; Mum's marker moves beside the high chair while your purchased chair stays where it was. Your ticket still reads 'Beside Mum.' An optional VIP photo panel shows the requested picture with both parents, followed by Mum's message asking you to photograph your siblings first. Its gallery preview shows you reflected in the glass cabinet behind them. A reachable Transfer panel lets you give the confirmed ticket to your sister, Lucy. Confirming removes it from your wallet and reveals Mum's message: 'Can you drive Lucy over?' Reset restores the original seating and ownership. Keep Choose seat, Continue, View photo package, Transfer ticket and Reset as plain controls.

hero.h1: You paid to meet your parents.
hero.sub: Turnout sells middle children tickets to family gatherings. Reserve the chair beside Mum and buy a photo with both parents. Mum has asked you to take it.

features.title: Choose the seat beside Mum.
features.blurb: Reserve the chair beside Mum so you can tell her about your promotion. Your brother arrives with the baby and she moves to the other end of the table. You tell her handbag.

features.title: Add a family photo.
features.blurb: The VIP package includes a picture with both parents. Mum hands you her phone and gathers your siblings for a quick one first. She likes that one best. It goes above the fireplace.

features.title: Transfer your ticket.
features.blurb: Your sister has had a difficult week. Give her your place at lunch in two taps, then explain how pleased you are that she can go. Mum asks you to drive her.

candidates.premise: Middle children buy tickets to family gatherings so their place in the family finally comes with a seat number.
candidates.audience_behavior: An overlooked adult wants visible proof of inclusion but still yields attention and opportunities to siblings.
candidates.source_mechanic: Event listings, reserved seating, VIP photo packages, mobile tickets and ticket transfers.
candidates.comic_turn: The buyer secures a chair while Mum moves away, purchases a photograph they end up taking, and transfers admission before becoming the replacement guest's driver.

candidates.premise: Middle children sell tickets to their own achievements and discover their parents will attend only if a sibling appears on the bill.
candidates.audience_behavior: Someone tries to make a promotion or birthday important enough for the family to attend.
candidates.source_mechanic: Event publishing, ticket sales, promotional offers and an event lineup.
candidates.comic_turn: Adding an older sibling's brief appearance sells the event, but the family leaves when that sibling does, before the achievement being celebrated.

candidates.premise: Middle children resell the family appearances they always agree to make, then find their own birthday listed among the unwanted tickets.
candidates.audience_behavior: The dependable sibling wants to escape obligatory visits without admitting they would rather stay home.
candidates.source_mechanic: Resale listings, asking prices, ticket ownership and transfers.
candidates.comic_turn: The attempt to escape family duties reveals that relatives classify spending time with the seller as another duty to offload.

angle_selection.reason: The first premise makes the familiar desire to be included immediately visible through a purchased seat. It supports three distinct reversals: proximity fails to secure attention, a photo purchase preserves the buyer's absence, and voluntary generosity turns the excluded guest into transport. The second risks repeating sibling upstaging in every feature; the third needs more explanation before the ticket exchange feels natural. Against the recent digest, this avoids collection growth, recurring matching-outfit payments, referral recruitment and administrative parody. The photograph hook concerns a paying subject becoming the photographer, rather than a product displacing a child in a retail review.
angle_selection.selected_premise: Middle children buy tickets to family gatherings so their place in the family finally comes with a seat number.

observations.behavior: An adult middle child thinks sitting beside Mum will finally provide a chance to talk about an achievement, while the family gravitates toward a sibling's baby.
observations.mechanic: A reserved-seating map sells the specific chair beside Mum and issues a ticket naming that location.
observations.consequence: The purchased chair remains guaranteed while Mum moves elsewhere. The customer delivers a promotion announcement to her handbag, then looks childish for insisting on staying in the seat they bought.
observations.landing_callback: The seating feature ends with the handbag receiving the news. Daniel's testimonial adds the public embarrassment of defending his isolation with a valid ticket.
observations.demo_callback: Selecting and booking the premium chair triggers the baby's arrival update. Mum's marker moves; the ticket retains 'Beside Mum,' and a handbag occupies her former chair.

observations.behavior: A middle child wants to appear in the family record but automatically accepts the phone when someone needs a photograph taken.
observations.mechanic: A VIP ticket bundles a scheduled photograph with both parents and delivery of the selected image.
observations.consequence: The buyer becomes the camera operator for the photograph chosen for permanent display. Their only accidental appearance is a reflection that Mum later crops out.
observations.landing_callback: The hero introduces the paid photo and Mum's request. The feature gives the resulting sibling photograph the fireplace position; Priya's testimonial extends its use to the Christmas card and removes her reflection.
observations.demo_callback: The photo-package panel starts with a request for a portrait with both parents. Mum's phone request leads to a gallery selection showing the buyer only in the cabinet reflection; a Christmas-card crop excludes that reflection.

observations.behavior: A middle child gives up a scarce place when a sibling has a problem and then volunteers enough reassurance to make the sacrifice look effortless.
observations.mechanic: A confirmed mobile ticket can be transferred to a named family member, removing admission from the original owner's wallet.
observations.consequence: The buyer loses their place and becomes the replacement guest's driver. The family sends an affectionate wish-you-were-here photograph to someone waiting immediately outside.
observations.landing_callback: The transfer feature ends with Mum assigning the lift. Helen's testimonial follows the trip through the meal and turns the family selfie into evidence of her nearby exclusion.
observations.demo_callback: Transferring the ticket to Lucy changes the wallet owner and reveals the pickup request. The completed transfer record includes a later family selfie captioned 'Wish you were here' and a return pickup time.

source_product_patterns: Discover upcoming events through dated listings with venue and ticket availability.
Open an event detail page with ticket categories and a prominent booking action.
Choose numbered seats from a map with price categories and unavailable positions.
Review the selected ticket and complete a short, explicit reservation flow.
Offer a VIP package combining admission with a scheduled photo opportunity.
Store a confirmed ticket in a mobile wallet with its seat and owner.
Transfer a ticket to a named recipient and update ownership visibly.
editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: Find a family event, leading to the Sunday Lunch booking screen. Recognizable product visual: an event detail page with a dining-table seat map, ticket categories and order summary. Open with the Turnout identity, a small the worst AI studio ever credit, the headline, explanation and CTA. Place the working ticket preview directly below so the chair beside Mum, its price and the booking action are visible together. Follow with three open feature passages, customer incidents and one joined ticket-category comparison. Proposed artwork one shows an adult remaining in a numbered dining chair beside a handbag while the rest of the family gathers around a baby's high chair at the other end; its purpose is to make the difference between owning a seat and receiving attention visible. Proposed artwork two shows a family posing before a glass-fronted cabinet, with the middle child holding the camera and appearing only in its reflection; its purpose is to explain the failed VIP photograph. A small family-home exterior thumbnail identifies the event venue. Keep ticket names, prices, messages, seat labels and photograph captions in live text. On mobile, stack event details, seating map, ticket category and summary in booking order. Artwork follows the usable preview.

references.reference: The extended Sunday-lunch table with borrowed folding chairs and a high chair squeezed into the best position
references.cues: Warm wood, cream tablecloth, tomato-colored serving dishes, mismatched chair silhouettes and a table stretched beyond its original proportions.
references.application: Use walnut text, warm cream surfaces and tomato-red booking controls. Draw the seating map as an actual household table with distinct dining, folding and high-chair shapes. The selected chair has a clear outline and number.

references.reference: Spiral-bound community cookbooks with family recipes and handwritten additions
references.cues: Readable domestic serif headings, practical sans-serif notes, generous recipe margins, thin dividing rules and occasional butter-yellow paper tabs.
references.application: Pair Literata display typography with Work Sans controls and body text. Use open editorial feature passages and straight rules. Butter-yellow tabs distinguish event details, tickets and photo information without turning the page into a scrapbook.

references.reference: A kitchen-wall family birthday calendar with extra names squeezed into occupied dates
references.cues: A clear printed date grid, uneven handwritten additions and names competing for limited space.
references.application: Use a restrained calendar strip for event discovery and one handwritten family update near the event listing. Keep all prices, controls and essential labels in typeset text. The calendar establishes whose occasion the family is attending.

audience_design.landing_application: Use cream backgrounds, walnut text, tomato-red primary actions and small butter-yellow highlights. Large domestic serif headlines sit above a broad, readable ticket-booking preview. Give the two campaign images distinct jobs: the first exposes the useless reserved chair; the second exposes the absent photo buyer. Use rectangular photographs and open text passages, with no portrait-package frames or decorative collage around functional information.
audience_design.demo_application: Retain the source service's event header, date and venue, selectable seat map, ticket categories, order summary, confirmation and ticket wallet. Carry the domestic typography and palette into that structure, using Work Sans for dense information and plain controls. The map uses household chairs instead of arena sections. Keep selections, ownership changes and family updates explicit; move Mum only after booking so the consequence follows the user's recognizable purchase.

Domestic table, calendar dates and place-setting ticket identity differ from twin portrait windows, chair pennant, bridge bands, poultry rosette, rail siding, yearbook and cupboard. items.prompt: Design a finished original logo for fictional family event ticket retailer "Turnout". Exact wordmark spelling: Turnout. Community cookbook domestic identity. Warm walnut #422C22 and tomato red #B83727 only on pure white #FFFFFF flat background for extraction. items.prompt: Create a finished graphic-design editorial campaign composition for Turnout, fictional tickets to family gatherings. Attached image is the APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE: preserve plate-and-ticket motif, walnut #422C22, tomato #B83727, cream #FFF8E9 and butter yellow #F0D377. A sophisticated illustrated spread from a spiral-bound community cookbook, gouache/cut-paper print texture, large clear serif typography, strong art direction. Exact headline at top left: "Your chair is still here." Exact small label by occupied chair: "Seat 4". NO other text. Main illustration: overhead-oblique long family lunch table; one adult middle child sits alone at the left beside a handbag on an empty chair, politely talking toward it; across at the far right Mum and the entire rest of the family cluster delightedly around a baby in a high chair. Show exaggerated long distance and obvious unused place settings in between. Integrate an oversized tomato ticket tab and cream plate geometry into the composition with deliberate whitespace. Rich human facial expressions, ordinary believable Sunday clothes. Designed graphic artwork with typography and intentional illustrative layout, NOT a photograph with a caption, NOT a UI screenshot or basic diagram. All composition contained, no clipped lettering. Crisp readable at 390px, no fine print, no extra copy or watermarks.
items.verdict: Accepted. Large exact headline and Seat 4 spelling; solitary adult, handbag and distant family/baby create an immediately readable reversal. Strong composed cookbook spread, not a captioned photograph.

items.prompt: Design a finished editorial graphic campaign artwork for Turnout, fictional VIP tickets to family gatherings. Attached image is the APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE; preserve plate-and-ticket language, warm serif lettering and exact walnut #422C22 tomato #B83727 butter yellow #F0D377 cream #FFF8E9 palette. Match a sophisticated community-cookbook gouache and cut-paper printed illustration. Exact large headline: "A photo with everyone." Exact smaller prominent subline: "Taken by you." NO other typography. Intentional graphic-design layout, headline across upper third with an illustrated family portrait scene in the lower two thirds, generous negative space and subtle plate/ticket paper forms. Mum, Dad and two adult siblings pose tightly together in front of a glass-fronted walnut cabinet in a domestic dining room. The adult middle child stands OUTSIDE the portrait group at the left holding up a phone to photograph them; that person appears ONLY in a narrow clear reflection in cabinet glass behind the group, with the phone visible. Use visually precise reflection storytelling: the image viewpoint is the phone camera so the photographer is not seen directly, only reflected in cabinet glass at left edge. Four happy family members pose, reflected photographer partly excluded. Lived-in home, tomato serving dish on shelf, warm believable people. Compose text, expressive illustration and hierarchy together as actual editorial graphic design, not a photograph with caption, not a UI screenshot, not a primitive diagram. Readable typography at mobile width, all elements contained, no extra copy or watermarks.
items.placement: Landing photo feature; derivative in demo photo preview
items.verdict: Accepted. Exact headline and subline; four family members pose while phone-holding photographer appears in left cabinet reflection. Hierarchy, expressive illustration and shared palette verified.
